title: Practice: drills
description: Short exercises, one per skill, to make the core lessons stick.
author: Strudel Workshop

tracks.title: Beginner drills
tracks.blurb: One short exercise per beginner skill: 2–4 minutes each.

tracks.title: Intermediate drills
tracks.blurb: One per intermediate skill: rhythm, harmony, sound design, effects.

tracks.title: Expert drills
tracks.blurb: Acid, arrangement and mixing, one move at a time.

lessons.title: Set the tempo
lessons.goal: Change the tempo of a loop, in BPM.
lessons.concept: Strudel counts cycles per minute, and our cycle is one bar of four beats, so a BPM becomes `setcpm(BPM/4)`.

tasks.text: Make it 128 BPM.

challenge.text: Slow it to 120 BPM, a deep house tempo.

summary: setcpm(BPM/4) sets the tempo.

lessons.title: Two bars, not one
lessons.goal: Write a kick pattern that changes every bar.
lessons.concept: Angle brackets `< >` pick one item per cycle, and each cycle is a bar. Put two patterns inside and you have a two-bar phrase.

tasks.text: Make the kick play four times in bar 1 and three times in bar 2.

challenge.text: Make it a four-bar phrase: 4, 4, 4, then 2 kicks.

summary: < > plays one item per bar, in turn.

lessons.title: Eighths and sixteenths
lessons.goal: Put closed hats on 8ths, then on 16ths.
lessons.concept: Everything in the quotes shares the bar. `hh*8` splits it into eight; `hh*16` into sixteen.

tasks.text: Make the hats play 8th notes.
Now 16th notes.

challenge.text: Write the 16ths as four groups of four, with brackets.

summary: *8 and *16 split the bar into 8ths and 16ths.
Brackets group steps.

lessons.title: Four on the floor, three ways
lessons.goal: Write the same four kicks three different ways.
lessons.concept: `bd*4`, `bd bd bd bd` and `bd!4` all play the same thing. Knowing that frees you to read other people’s code.

tasks.text: Four kicks with *4.
Now write them out as four words.

challenge.text: And a third way, with !.

summary: *n, spelling it out and !n all mean the same four kicks.

lessons.title: Kick, clap, hats
lessons.goal: Build the classic house kit from nothing.
lessons.concept: Kick on every beat, clap on 2 and 4, open hat on every offbeat: the whole kit in three lines.
lessons.starter: setcpm(124/4)

tasks.text: A part called kick: four on the floor, TR-909.
A part called clap on beats 2 and 4, and stack it.
A part called hats: an open hat on every offbeat, quiet.

summary: Kick on the beats, clap on 2 and 4, open hat on the offbeats.

lessons.title: Find the offbeat
lessons.goal: Put hits halfway between the beats.
lessons.concept: The offbeat is the "and": `[~ oh]` is a rest then a hat, so `[~ oh]*4` lands on every "and".

tasks.text: Move the open hats to the offbeats.

challenge.text: Add closed hats only on the "and" of 2 and the "and" of 4.

summary: [~ x] puts x on the offbeat.

lessons.title: Leave a gap
lessons.goal: Take hits out of a pattern with rests.
lessons.concept: A `~` is silence for one step. Removing a hit is often the better edit.

tasks.text: Rest on beat 2.

challenge.text: Rest on beats 2 and 4, written with - instead of ~.

summary: ~ (or -) is a rest.

lessons.title: Swap the machine
lessons.goal: Move a beat between the 909, the 808 and the 707.
lessons.concept: The names stay (bd, cp, hh); only `.bank` changes, so one beat can wear many machines.

tasks.text: Put the kick on the TR-808.
And the clap on the TR-707.

challenge.text: Add TR-606 closed hats on the offbeats.

summary: .bank("…") picks the machine; the sound names stay.

lessons.title: Layers
lessons.goal: Add parts to a stack, one at a time.
lessons.concept: `stack(a, b, c)` plays its parts together. Every track is layers.

tasks.text: Add offbeat open hats as a third part.
tasks.hint: const hats = s("[~ oh]*4").bank("RolandTR909").gain(.5), then stack(kick, clap, hats)

tasks.text: Add a fourth: a rimshot on the last 16th of each beat.

summary: stack(…) layers parts; add a name to add a layer.

lessons.title: Levels
lessons.goal: Balance the parts with gain and velocity.
lessons.concept: `.gain` sets a part’s level (0–1). `.velocity` is per hit, so a pattern of velocities makes accents.

tasks.text: Turn the hats down to .4.
Give the clap a velocity pattern: the second clap harder.

summary: .gain is the part’s level; .velocity is per hit.

lessons.title: Notes and octaves
lessons.goal: Name notes, and move them by an octave.
lessons.concept: Notes are letters plus an octave number: c2 is low, c3 an octave higher. eb is E flat.

tasks.text: Drop the note an octave, to c2.
Alternate c2 and eb2.

challenge.text: Play the same two notes an octave up.

summary: c2, eb2, c3: letter, accidental, octave.

lessons.title: The offbeat bass
lessons.goal: Write a bass that plays between the kicks.
lessons.concept: Kick on the beat, bass on the offbeat: the two never collide, and the groove bounces.

tasks.text: Add a part called bass: a sawtooth c2 on every offbeat.
tasks.hint: const bass = note("[~ c2]*4").s("sawtooth"), and stack it

challenge.text: Make the last bass note a g1.

summary: [~ c2]*4 puts the bass between the kicks.

lessons.title: Samples and synths
lessons.goal: Mix a sampled drum with synthesized tones.
lessons.concept: `s("bd")` plays a recording. `s("square")` or `s("sawtooth")` generates a tone from a waveform, and needs a note to play.

tasks.text: Add a part called tone: a square wave playing c2 on every beat.
tasks.hint: const tone = note("c2*4").s("square"), and stack it

tasks.text: Change the waveform to sawtooth.

challenge.text: Add a sampled piano playing c4 on beat 1.

summary: Samples are recordings; synths are waveforms that need a note.

lessons.title: Darker
lessons.goal: Close a low-pass filter on a bass.
lessons.concept: A low-pass filter keeps the lows and cuts above the cutoff. Lower cutoff, darker sound.

tasks.text: Bring the cutoff down to 400 Hz.

challenge.text: Open and close it every other bar: 400, then 1200.

summary: .lpf(hz): lower is darker.
A pattern in quotes changes the cutoff per bar.

lessons.title: Shuffle
lessons.goal: Swing a row of 16th hats like an MPC.
lessons.concept: `.swingBy(x, 8)` delays every second 16th. For an MPC swing of p%, x = (p − 50) / 50: 57% is .14.

tasks.text: Swing the hats to about 57%.

challenge.text: Push it to a triplet feel, 62–63%.

summary: .swingBy(x, 8): x = (swing% − 50) / 50.

lessons.title: Syncopate the clap
lessons.goal: Move a hit off the beat to make the groove lean.
lessons.concept: Syncopation is an accent where you don’t expect one. Pushing the last clap to the "and" of 4 pulls the bar forward.

tasks.text: Move the second clap to the "and" of beat 4.

challenge.text: Add a rimshot on the "and" of 2 only.

summary: An accent off the beat gives a groove tension.

lessons.title: Euclidean rhythm
lessons.goal: Spread hits evenly with (k,n) and rotate them.
lessons.concept: `rim(3,8)` spreads 3 hits over 8 steps as evenly as possible. A third number rotates the pattern.

tasks.text: Make the rim play 3 hits over 8 steps.
Rotate it by one step so it starts off the beat.

challenge.text: Add a cowbell with 5 hits over 16 steps.

summary: x(k,n,rot): k hits over n steps, rotated.

lessons.title: Ghost notes
lessons.goal: Add quiet in-between hits that you feel more than hear.
lessons.concept: A gain pattern makes some 16ths loud and some barely there. Ghost notes fill the groove without crowding it.

tasks.text: Give the hats a gain pattern: loud on the beat, ghosts between.

challenge.text: Add a ghost snare on the last 16th of beats 2 and 4, very quiet.

summary: A gain pattern per step makes accents and ghosts.

lessons.title: Scale degrees
lessons.goal: Write a line in a key with scale degrees, then change the key.
lessons.concept: `n("0 2 4").scale("C3:minor")` picks the 1st, 3rd and 5th notes of C minor. Change the scale name and the whole line moves.

tasks.text: Rewrite the lead as scale degrees of C minor.
Move it to A minor by changing only the scale.

summary: n(…).scale("A3:minor"): degrees of a key, octave in the name.

lessons.title: Build a chord
lessons.goal: Stack notes into a minor seventh.
lessons.concept: Commas inside a step play notes together. C, E♭, G is C minor; add B♭ for the classic house minor 7th.

tasks.text: Make it a C minor triad.
Add the seventh, bb3.

challenge.text: Write the same chord by name, with a voicing.

summary: Commas stack notes; chord("Cm7").voicing() names them.

lessons.title: Two chords
lessons.goal: Alternate chords across bars, then make a four-bar progression.
lessons.concept: `chord("<Cm7 Fm7>")` picks one chord per bar. Four chords in the brackets make a four-bar progression.

tasks.text: Alternate Cm7 and Fm7 every bar.

challenge.text: Make it four bars: Cm7, Fm7, Ab^7, Gm7.

summary: < > over chord names: one chord per bar.

lessons.title: Out of the kick’s way
lessons.goal: Move the bass off the beats and shorten it.
lessons.concept: Kick and bass share the low end. Put the bass between the kicks and keep each note short so they never overlap.

tasks.text: Move the bass to the offbeats.
Make each note a short pluck.

summary: Bass between the kicks, short, never on top of them.

lessons.title: Swap the waveform
lessons.goal: Hear sine, square and supersaw on the same line.
lessons.concept: Sine is pure, square is hollow, sawtooth is buzzy, supersaw is several saws detuned into a wide wall.

tasks.text: Make it a square wave.
Now a supersaw with seven voices.

challenge.text: Spread the supersaw’s voices wider.

summary: sine, square, sawtooth, supersaw: same notes, different colour.

lessons.title: Pad to pluck
lessons.goal: Shape a sound with its envelope.
lessons.concept: Attack is the fade-in, release the fade-out. A fast decay with no sustain turns any pad into a pluck.

tasks.text: Make it a slow pad: a long attack and release.
Now a pluck with .adsr: no attack, short decay, no sustain.
tasks.hint: .adsr("0:.15:0:.1") instead of the attack and release

summary: Attack and release make a pad; .adsr("a:d:s:r") sets all four.

lessons.title: Squelch
lessons.goal: Add resonance to a filtered bass.
lessons.concept: Resonance boosts the frequencies right at the cutoff. Turn it up and the filter starts to sing.

tasks.text: Set the resonance to 15.

challenge.text: Make the cutoff move with a pattern so the resonance sweeps.

summary: .lpq(0–50): resonance at the cutoff.

lessons.title: Thin it out
lessons.goal: High-pass the hats and the clap to clear the low end.
lessons.concept: A high-pass filter removes lows. Hats and claps carry no useful bass, so cutting it leaves room for the kick.

tasks.text: High-pass the hats at 400 Hz.
And the clap at 200 Hz.

summary: .hpf(hz) removes lows; use it on everything but kick and bass.

lessons.title: The filter wow
lessons.goal: Put an envelope on the cutoff.
lessons.concept: `.lpenv` opens the filter on each note by that many octaves; `.lpdecay` says how fast it closes again. That is the 303 "wow".

tasks.text: Add a filter envelope: depth 4, decay .15.

challenge.text: Vary the depth per note: deeper on the first of each beat.

summary: .lpenv(depth) + .lpdecay(s): a filter envelope per note.

lessons.title: Room
lessons.goal: Put the clap in a room.
lessons.concept: `.room` is how much reverb a sound gets. A touch pushes it back; a lot puts it in a hall.

tasks.text: Give the clap a little reverb.

challenge.text: Now a big hall: room .8 or more.

summary: .room(0–1): reverb amount.

lessons.title: The dotted echo
lessons.goal: Give a stab a tempo-synced delay.
lessons.concept: `.delaysync(3/16)` is a dotted-eighth echo, the classic dub spacing. `.delayfeedback` is how many repeats.

tasks.text: Add a dotted-eighth delay to the stab.

challenge.text: Let it ring: feedback .7.

summary: .delaysync(3/16): dotted-eighth echoes in time.

lessons.title: Grit
lessons.goal: Overdrive a bass and crush a clap.
lessons.concept: `.distort` overdrives a sound for harmonics; `.crush` lowers the bit depth for a 12-bit crunch.

tasks.text: Overdrive the bass.
Crush the clap to 6 bits.

summary: .distort for drive, .crush for lo-fi bits.

lessons.title: Left and right
lessons.goal: Place percussion in the stereo field.
lessons.concept: `.pan(0)` is hard left, 1 hard right, .5 centre. Keep kick, bass and clap in the middle; move the small stuff.

tasks.text: Pan the open hats a little left.
Bounce the rim left and right with a pattern.

summary: .pan(0–1): left to right; patterns bounce it.

lessons.title: Breathe
lessons.goal: Move a cutoff with a slow sine.
lessons.concept: A signal like `sine` goes 0 to 1 and back. `.range(300, 1500).slow(4)` turns it into a cutoff that breathes over 4 bars.

tasks.text: Replace the fixed cutoff with a 4-bar sine between 300 and 1500 Hz.

challenge.text: Use perlin for a wandering cutoff instead.

summary: signal.range(a, b).slow(n): an LFO on any control.

lessons.title: Every fourth bar
lessons.goal: Change the loop on the last bar of four.
lessons.concept: `.lastOf(4, f)` applies f in the last bar of every four. `x => x.ply(2)` doubles every hit: an instant fill.

tasks.text: Double the hats on the last bar of every four.

challenge.text: Drop the clap in that same bar.

summary: .lastOf(n, f) changes the last bar of n; .mask silences bars.

lessons.title: Pick and tune
lessons.goal: Choose a sample variation and tune it.
lessons.concept: Most machines have several kicks: `.n(1)` picks the second. `.speed` pitches a sample: below 1 is lower and longer.

tasks.text: Pick the second 909 kick.
Tune it down a little.

summary: .n picks a variation; .speed tunes a sample.

lessons.title: The acid voice
lessons.goal: Turn a saw line into a 303.
lessons.concept: Ladder filter, high resonance, a short filter envelope: the three things that make a sawtooth sound like a 303.

tasks.text: Ladder filter, resonance 18, filter envelope 4 with decay .15.
Accent three steps with a velocity pattern.

summary: Ladder + resonance + filter envelope = 303.
Accents are a velocity pattern.

lessons.title: The long sweep
lessons.goal: Open a filter over 16 bars.
lessons.concept: `saw.range(300, 3000).slow(16)` rises for 16 bars and drops back. On the cutoff it is the acid build.

tasks.text: Replace the fixed cutoff with a 16-bar saw from 300 to 3000 Hz.

challenge.text: Sweep the resonance too, on an 8-bar sine.

summary: saw.range(a, b).slow(16): a 16-bar rise.

lessons.title: Sections
lessons.goal: Name two sections and arrange them.
lessons.concept: A section is a stack with a name. `arrange([4, intro], [8, main])` plays them in turn, for that many bars each.

tasks.text: Name an intro (kick and hats) and a main (everything); keep playing main.
tasks.hint: const intro = stack(kick, hats), const main = stack(kick, clap, hats, bass), then main

tasks.text: Arrange 4 bars of intro, then 8 of main.

summary: Sections are named stacks; arrange() plays them in order.

lessons.title: Build and drop
lessons.goal: A riser and a roll into the drop.
lessons.concept: A noise riser with a rising high-pass, and a snare roll (`.ply(4)`) in the last bar, tell the floor the drop is coming.

tasks.text: Add a part called riser: pink noise with a high-pass rising over 4 bars.
Roll the clap in the last bar of four.

summary: A rising high-pass on noise is a riser; .ply(4) on the last bar is a roll.

lessons.title: DJ-friendly
lessons.goal: Drums-only in and out, the full groove between.
lessons.concept: A DJ needs bars of plain drums at each end to mix. Three sections: intro, main, outro.

tasks.text: Add an outro of kick and hats, 4 bars, after main.
tasks.hint: const outro = stack(kick, hats), then arrange([4, intro], [8, main], [4, outro])

challenge.text: Bring the clap in halfway through the intro with a mask.

summary: Intro and outro of drums; .mask brings parts in on a bar.

lessons.title: Pump
lessons.goal: Duck the bass under the kick.
lessons.concept: Sidechain: the kick ducks whatever is on the target orbit. Put the bass on orbit 2 and point the kick at it.

tasks.text: Put the bass on orbit 2.
Make the kick duck orbit 2, depth .8.

summary: .duckorbit(n) on the kick ducks what plays on orbit n.

lessons.title: Squash
lessons.goal: Compress a clap for punch.
lessons.concept: `.compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release")` evens out a sound per voice. Strudel has no master compressor (gap G6).

tasks.text: Compress the clap.

summary: .compressor("thr:ratio:knee:att:rel"), per voice.

lessons.title: Headroom
lessons.goal: Bring a loud mix down so the kick stays on top.
lessons.concept: Nothing above gain 1, and nothing louder than the kick. Turn parts down, never the kick up.

tasks.text: Bring every part to 1 or below.
Make sure nothing is louder than the kick.
tasks.hint: the kick at .9 is the loudest; keep clap and hats below it

summary: Gain ≤ 1 everywhere; the kick on top.

lessons.title: Its own orbit
lessons.goal: Give each effected part its own bus.
lessons.concept: Strudel has one delay and one reverb per orbit. Two parts on one orbit with different settings overwrite each other.

tasks.text: Move the stab to orbit 2 so its delay is its own.
And the clap to orbit 3.

summary: One reverb and one delay per orbit: effected parts get their own.

lessons.title: Never the same
lessons.goal: Thin out the hats at random, repeatably.
lessons.concept: `.degradeBy(.3)` drops 30% of the hits at random. `.seed(n)` picks which random, so it is the same every time.

tasks.text: Drop about a third of the hats at random.
Pin the randomness with a seed.

challenge.text: Sometimes pitch a hat up an octave.

summary: .degradeBy drops hits; .seed makes random repeatable.
